title: Measurement and Geometry - Lesson 8 Practice: Square Pyramid Volume
description: Practice finding square pyramid volume using base side length, vertical height, and correct cubic units.

questions.question: Which formula finds the volume of a square pyramid with base side length s and vertical height h?
questions.explanation: A square pyramid has one-third the volume of a square prism with the same base area and height, so V = (1/3)s^2h.

questions.question: A square pyramid has base side length 6 cm and vertical height 9 cm. What is its volume?
A square pyramid has side length 3 m and vertical height 12 m. Enter the volume as a number only.
The slant height of a square pyramid is always the height used in the volume formula.
questions.explanation: Volume uses vertical height, the straight distance from the base to the top vertex. Slant height runs along a triangular face.

questions.question: A square pyramid has base side length 10 ft and vertical height 6 ft. Which setup correctly finds its volume?
questions.explanation: The base area is s^2, so the correct setup is V = (1/3)(10^2)(6).

questions.question: A square pyramid has base area 64 in^2 and vertical height 15 in. What is its volume?
A square pyramid has base side length 9 cm and vertical height 4 cm. Enter the volume as a number only.
A square pyramid problem gives vertical height 7 cm and slant height 11 cm. Which height should be used for volume, and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Use the vertical height, 7 cm, because the volume formula uses the straight height perpendicular to the base, not the slant height along a side face.
questions.explanation: The vertical height measures the prism-like height used in V = (1/3)Bh. Slant height is not used for volume.
